overall.summary: Two units are wrong: the Asian or Pacific Islander part's plain hypothesis says it raises the chance of a low income when the model lowers it, and the private household service technical hypothesis gives 287 rows where there are 187. The share of zero capital gains is overstated (95% vs 91.6%). Everything else reproduces.

findings.statement: This part raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) a little for Asian or Pacific Islander people.
findings.check: direction against the cited claim C103, the part's closed form and a probe over race at the typical case
findings.evidence: The part lowers it. C103 gives -0.148 log-odds (odds ratio 0.862), 62% -> 58%; probe: race=4 (White) 61.9%, race=1 (Asian or Pacific Islander) 58.4%, part contribution -0.144 vs +0.005. The part's own plain evidence sentence, the summary block and the technical hypothesis all say 'lowers' / 'negative offset'.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --sweep race=all

findings.statement: 11966=relu(1.0045*occ9-0.516+0.968*2197) is 13.97 for the 287 occupation:9 rows (+1.40 logit), else 0.
findings.check: subgroup count of occupation:9 (private household service) on train
findings.evidence: n = 187 of 39073 (185 with income <= $50K), not 287. The part's own evidence record and the plain text say 187. The value 13.97 and +1.40 logit reproduce (standardised one-hot 14.42 x 1.0045 - 0.516 = 13.97; x 0.1003 = 1.401; subgroup mean contribution 1.401).
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --where "occupation == '9'"

findings.statement: +0.41 logit at cg=0 (95% of rows) (also in operations.capital_gain_penalty.evidence[1])
findings.check: subgroup count of capital-gain == 0 on train
findings.evidence: Zero capital gain is 35788 of 39073 rows = 91.6%, not 95%. The +0.406 value at 0 reproduces (probe exit 0.406). Everything else in the hypothesis holds (see V5).
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --where "`capital-gain` == 0"

findings.statement: concave piecewise-linear penalty, slope -2.79/sd then -5.71/sd, kink z=0.554 (~5.2k USD), -73.7 at 99,999 USD; ablation AUC 0.9078->0.8896, acc 0.852->0.832
findings.check: probe sweep of capital gains; hand calculation from the closed form; subgroup above the kink; mean ablation
findings.evidence: Probe exits: 0.406 at 0, -1.45 at 5000, -1.55 at 5250, -1.74 at 5500, -2.12 at 6000: about 0.372 logit per 1000 USD below and 0.762 above (ratio 2.05 = 5.71/2.79); kink between 5250 and 5500 USD. Closed form at max z 13.19 gives -73.75. capital-gain > 5247: 1757 rows = 4.50%, matching '9352 active on 4.50%'. Ablation to mean: AUC 0.9078 -> 0.8896, accuracy 0.8520 -> 0.8319. Capital gain is not a direct root input, so 'whole effect' holds.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --sweep capital-gain=0,1000,2000,3000,4000,5000,5250,5500,6000,6849,8000,10000
uv run python -m explaneat verify ablate experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --part capital_gain_penalty --to mean
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --where "`capital-gain` > 5247"

findings.statement: lowers the predicted chance as capital gains rise, slowly at first, then faster
findings.check: probe sweep 0 to 10,000 USD at the typical case
findings.evidence: Risk 61.9% (0) -> 52.9% (1000) -> 20.2% (5000) -> 6.4% (6849) -> 0.6% (10,000); log-odds slope doubles past ~5.25k USD. Matches the plain hypothesis and evidence.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-ec520f --sweep capital-gain=0,1000,2000,3000,4000,5000,5250,5500,6000,6849,8000,10000
